correctness.rationale: Unrolling proves validity independent of all cycle lengths exceeding modal depth; surjective cyclic bounded morphisms prove divisor closure. Independent propositional letters realize each divisor-closed spectrum with matching optimal depth. Disjoint cycle decomposition and the labelled exponential formula prove the exact probability and recurrence. A positive-coefficient bound at radius \(n^{1/L}\) and the explicit all-L-cycle-plus-fixed-points contribution prove the two-sided logarithmic rate, including \(L=1\). Local finite checker reproduced the cyclic truth tables and permutation counts. Finite tests are corroboration, not proof of unbounded claims.

Müller, Skerman and Verstraaten, arXiv:2302.10148v3, Theorem 1.1(i) and Section 2 discuss Compton’s classical result: for uniform permutations in the first-order theory of one bijection, there is a convergence law but not a zero-one law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing restricted-permutation theorems dominate bare enumeration and are treated as prior art. They do not entail which length sets are definable by basic-modal frame validity, the divisor-closure restriction or the sharp modal depth. More expressive PDL results and unrestricted-frame limiting logic have different domains and validity versus satisfiability quantifiers. In particular, the stronger first-order language has nontrivial limits for uniform permutations, whereas universal-valuation basic-modal frame validity collapses to a zero-one law. These are distinct definability classes, and the general first-order convergence theorem does not imply the precise modal spectrum or sharp rate.

originality.rationale: The submitted claim is the exact basic-modal finite-cycle validity spectrum and sharp definability depth, together with its induced uniform-permutation probability hierarchy. The counted restrictions and much of their asymptotics are already developed in classical random-permutation literature; they are not asserted as novel independently. The motivating cyclic PDL paper concerns a richer language and satisfiability, not this cycle-validity spectrum. Searches found related general frame-validity zero-one questions and functional modal algebra, but no statement whose hypotheses and conclusion entail the precise characterization. Residual possibility of a classical equivalent characterization is openly acknowledged.
residual_risks: An older specialist article may state the same modal finite-cycle spectrum and optimal-depth classification in another language or as an immediate corollary of a previously developed algebraic theory.
Some related older papers and repository full documents were not accessible and only their summaries or abstracts could be compared.
The restricted-permutation counting identity and most coefficient asymptotics are classical; originality must not be ascribed to them independently.

value.rationale: This solves the naturally motivated classification of exactly which finite cycle spectra can be prescribed by universal-valuation validity in the simplest modal language, gives a sharp minimum nesting depth, and translates the classification into a complete family of sharply distinct random-frame decay exponents. The value is a complete structural boundary for what ordinary modal logic can and cannot distinguish among cycles; the classical probability formulas are a useful consequence rather than an invented independent discovery.
